Theme

Latin word

forte

adverb (the ablative of fors)

by chance, as it happened

In this lexicon

  • happen

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā; Cic. Planc. 65: Puteolōs forte vēnissem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 289; Traupman 325

Notes

  1. 1forte: short final e (Lewis & Short fortē). The ablative of the third-declension fors (de Vaan 236, s.v. fors: “abl. forte ‘by chance’”). Verg. A. 1.377, forte suā Libycīs tempestās adpulit ōrīs, and Hor. S. 1.9.1, ībam forte viā Sacrā: in both, forte su- and forte vi- are dactyls.

Examples

  • Ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs

    I happened to be walking along the Sacred Way, as is my habitHor. S. 1.9.1

    In the entry for happen

  • erat forte brūmae tempus et nivālis diēs

    it happened to be midwinter, and a snowy dayLiv. 21.54.7

    In the entry for happen

  • ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat

    as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand and shortens his stepQuint. 2.3.7

    In the entry for happen

  • Forte eum cōnspexī.

    I just happened to spot him.Traupman 325

    In the entry for happen
